item.title: Surviving Dementia Care: The Realities of Family Caregiving - Author Talk — Sat Oct 10, 2:00 PM — Locke
item.description:
Surviving Dementia Care is a compassionate and insightful guide for anyone navigating the challenging journey of caring for a loved one with dementia. Drawing on research from information studies, literary studies, and interviews with family caregivers, this book reimagines dementia care – not as a set of skills to master, but as a deeply human experience to endure and understand. ​Author and Professor Emeritus D. Grant Campbell will address the experiences of families who are caring for a loved one who is living with dementia, including the various points of stress, as well as the various points of joy, and ways in which caregivers learn to survive the experience. Major topics include understanding the diagnosis, communicating with the loved one, choosing an assisted living facility, and using music and the arts as a means of connection.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Adults

item.title: Autumn Awe at Crawford Lake — Sun Oct 11, 9:00 AM
item.description: Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club **Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/crawford-lake-26)** **Crawford Lake keeps its secrets in its sediment. We’ll share some of them with you on this adventure.** This emerald green meromictic lake is a scientific marvel. It’s so still that its deep layers never mix, and nothing that settles to the bottom ever gets disturbed. That untouched geological record, laid down year by year, is part of why it’s so special. We’ll follow the lake’s shores on the newly completed boardwalk, with radiant fall colours towering above us. From the lake, the trail climbs onto the Niagara Escarpment and joins the Bruce Trail, the longest trail network in Ontario. This section has some moderately technical terrain that will ask you to slow down and pay attention. item.title: Toronto Railway Museum - Model Trains: Not Just Toys Anymore — Tue Oct 13, 7:00 PM — online
item.description: Bill Schneider, one of the senior product designers at Rapido Trains Inc., will discuss how today’s model trains are researched, developed, and produced. Topics will include archival research, model mold production, decoration and assembly, as well as the role electronics play in today’s models. Rapido Trains, a Canadian company based in Markham, has been producing model trains in HO and N scales for more than 22 years. The company’s trains have earned a reputation among enthusiasts for their accurate detailing and exceptional quality. Rapido is also known for selecting projects that other manufacturers often overlook. About our speaker: Bill has been involved in the hobby industry since 1982, working in retail, wholesale, and manufacturing. He lives in central Connecticut. item.title: *FULL -Human Connection 101 Workshop Series for Seniors — Thu Oct 15, 1:30 PM — Fairview
item.description:
Human connection has a profound impact on our health and happiness, especially in our increasingly disconnected world. Join GenWell in an interactive 5-week (Oct 1, 8, 15, 22 & 29) program series to learn practical ways to enhance social health, understand the adverse effects of loneliness, and discover the benefits of building more meaningful connections. Receive a free social health workbook, spend time with other participants after the workshops, and enjoy some light refreshments provided. About GenWell: Founded in 2016, GenWell is a registered charity whose mission is to make the world a happier and healthier place by educating, empowering, and catalyzing forty million Canadians about the importance of their social health. Registration full.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Older Adults

item.title: homesick: on the way home — Thu Oct 15, 6:00 PM — STACKT market
item.description:
Address: STACKT market Toronto, ON Canada
kingston candle started at queen’s university. five years later, we’re on the way home. join us in toronto for the launch of homesick, the latest candle inspired by leaving home, finding somewhere new, and eventually realizing what you miss about where you came from. come meet someone you haven’t seen since kingston. or bring someone who’s never been. have a drink, smell homesick, shop kingston candle, and leave your mark on our map of where everyone calls home. if you never made it to kingston, now’s your chance. october 15, 2026 6–9 pm milky’s cloud room at stackt market toronto,…
Hosted by Kingston Candle

item.title: Youth Hub: Rolling in the Hub with Dungeons and Dragons — Fri Oct 16, 4:00 PM — Northern District
item.description: Fight fearsome goblins, discover ancient treasures and explore a fantasy world with your friends in the Youth Hub! Join us for a fun and collaborative storytelling experience led by a youth hub librarian as the game master. Registration for this program is required as space is limited. Program is hosted twice a month in the Youth Hub and participants must register for each individual session they wish to join. For teens only. No prior experience is required and new players are welcome to play. Dice and pre-generated character sheets will be provided for all participants. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more.
